title: Athena Query Execution Failures and Bytes Scanned

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `aws:cloudtrail` events with `eventName="StartQueryExecution" errorCode!=""` into `index=aws`. Confirm UC-4.1.48 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `aws:cloudtrail` traffic without `eventName="StartQueryExecution" errorCode!=""`. Confirm UC-4.1.48 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:cloudtrail` collected via `Splunk_TA_aws`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" eventName="StartQueryExecution" errorCode!=""
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress awsRegion
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.48_athena_query_execution_f_48"
| sort -_time
description: UC-4.1.48 — Athena Query Execution Failures and Bytes Scanned: queries AWS `aws:cloudtrail` for `StartQueryExecution` and returns actor, resource, and region context for performance review and change validation.
value: On AWS, `StartQueryExecution` activity for 'Athena Query Execution Failures and Bytes Scanned' is a high-signal control-plane change that should match approved change records and privileged-access monitoring. UC-4.1.48 drives medium-priority performance alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: Use CloudTrail for Athena API calls (success/failure). Optionally export query execution IDs and join with GetQueryExecution for bytes scanned and state. Alert on high failure rate or queries scanning >1TB.
visualization: Table (query, user, bytes, state), Line chart (bytes scanned over time), Bar chart (top users by bytes).
cimSpl:
| tstats `summariesonly` count
  from datamodel=Change.All_Changes
  where (All_Changes.action="failure" OR match(All_Changes.status, "(?i)error|AccessDenied|Invalid"))
     AND (match(All_Changes.app, "(?i)athena") OR match(All_Changes.object, "(?i)query|athena"))
  by All_Changes.user All_Changes.object span=1h
| sort -count

knownFalsePositives: Analysts stopping large queries, bad SQL in a lab, and role tests that you expect to fail in sandboxes.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_aws` with the modular input for `aws:cloudtrail`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.1.78.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Use CloudTrail for Athena API calls (success/failure). Optionally export query execution IDs and join with GetQueryExecution for bytes scanned and state. Alert on high failure rate or queries scanning >1TB.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" eventName="StartQueryExecution" errorCode!=""
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress awsRegion
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.48_athena_query_execution_f_48"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:cloudtrail` in `index=aws` to detect athena query execution failures and bytes scanned. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the AWS CloudTrail console Event history for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_1_48_alert` with severity aligned to `medium` criticality. Dashboard: Table (query, user, bytes, state), Line chart (bytes scanned over time), Bar chart (top users by bytes)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_aws` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of athena query execution failures and bytes scanned so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
